name: Protected Depth Is Unbounded Even on Reduced Terminal Obstructions
statement: For every $m\ge1$ there is an ample pc-minimal obstruction $L_m$ to dismantlable ampleness with $|L_m|=253\cdot2^m+121$, isometric dimension $m+23$, VC dimension $m+5$, empty protected core, and $d_{\mathrm{prot}}(L_m)\ge2^m$. Every one-coordinate reduction of $L_m$ peels. Its minimum graph degree is at least three and its signed minimal-nonface columns are pairwise distinct up to sign, so it is fixed by both canonical graph-core and column-compression reductions.
proof: Replace one active root direction inside a rooted factor, use rooted-block transfer and frozen missing-cube witnesses, glue it to a second factor, and complete their mixed root cube. Add the punctured fibre of a three-support tip. Every tip subset is nonpeelable: frozen witnesses block factor vertices, mixed root-cube supports control mixed vertices, root deletion exposes a protected old set, and any other first corner only removes a tip. Equal-support extension makes the full tip set ample and relatively peelable to the negative base, while the one-concept atlas gives forbiddenness and positive reductions throughout. The whole fibre-deletion branch has empty protected core, proving the depth bound. Degree counting proves minimum degree three, and cross-factor missing pairs distinguish every signed clause column.
